text:
Connor O'Brien: heads up: need to lock SDK version targets for the streaming/tool-calling/structured-output examples refresh. also need final changelog blurbs + whether we’re backporting any of the example fixes. can folks drop proposed versions + readiness?

Monica Patel: Python side: PRs in flight/merged:
- redwood-sdk-python#2874 (examples refresh)
- #2881 (golden tests)
- #2890 (structured-output helpers + docs strings)
All are green on main. We can cut a minor.

Dana Lo: TS side: merged:
- redwood-sdk-typescript#1932 (tool calling types + examples)
- #1940 (streaming handler refactor)
- #1951 (structured output JSON schema example)
No API surface change beyond typing + examples, but it’s not just a doc tweak. I’d prefer minor.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go: merged:
- redwood-sdk-go#744 streaming consumer loop update
- #752 tool calling example + fixtures
- #761 structured output example + JSON validation
All behind examples/ directory + internal helper. No breaking changes.

Ibrahim Khan: +1 on minor bumps across the board. the “canonical” event naming is consistent in examples now. would like to avoid patch release implying “bugfix” only.

Connor O'Brien: ok. can we propose concrete versions?

Monica Patel: Python currently at v1.11.2. propose v1.12.0 for examples refresh + golden tests.

Dana Lo: TS currently v0.22.3. propose v0.23.0.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go currently v0.8.6. propose v0.9.0.

Brian Murphy: sanity: any chance these examples rely on unreleased API behavior? (esp streaming tool-call partial args + final assembly corner case)

Sabrina James: examples were updated to use only released semantics. there’s a note in python/ts/go examples: partial tool args may arrive over multiple deltas; assemble before JSON.parse/unmarshal.

Ibrahim Khan: also note: no new event types were introduced. examples handle the existing stream events + tolerate disconnects.

Sahana Iyer: re golden tests: Python fixtures are stable in CI now. but we should call out in release notes that fixtures are “example-level transcripts” and might change if backend formatting changes. (we’ve pinned normalization rules)

Connor O'Brien: cool. need changelog copy. pls drop suggested bullets in-thread.

Monica Patel: Python changelog draft:
- Examples: refreshed streaming + tool calling snippets to match canonical event model.
- Examples: added structured output (JSON schema) sample with validation helpers.
- Tests: added golden transcript tests for streaming tool-call sequences.
- Docs: clarified retry/disconnect handling and partial tool arguments in streaming.

Dana Lo: TS changelog draft:
- Examples: updated streaming example to assemble deltas consistently and handle tool-call argument streaming.
- Types: improved tool calling typings for tool definitions/results; fixes mismatch in prior snippet shape.
- Examples: added structured output JSON schema example + runtime validation.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go changelog draft:
- Examples: refreshed streaming consumer loop and added helper for assembling final response.
- Examples: added tool calling example (incl parallel tool call loop) + fixtures.
- Examples: added structured output example with JSON validation + retry guidance.

Elliot Price: docs site is shipping separately via redwood-docs PRs 512/519/527/534. please include “docs updated” links in SDK release notes? ideally point at /guides/streaming, /guides/tool-calling, /guides/structured-output.

Wei Chen: +1. and we should note model variability + support matrix language (PM sign-off). I can provide final URLs once redirects are merged.

Connor O'Brien: backports: do we need to patch older versions? support asked for TS type mismatch fix.

Dana Lo: for TS, the type mismatch issue (SUP-18452) is resolved by #1932. we can backport to v0.22.x as v0.22.4 (patch) if we want to minimize upgrade friction. but the examples on docs will reference v0.23.0.

Monica Patel: python: i’d avoid backport unless there’s a customer-impacting bug. this is mostly examples/tests. we can do v1.11.3 patch *only* if support wants it, but i don’t think necessary.

Mateusz Zielinski: go: no backport requested. +1 to “no backports unless ticket demands.”

Brian Murphy: i’d support TS patch backport only, since it fixes a real compile error for folks copy/pasting older snippet. doesn’t change runtime.

Sahana Iyer: if we backport TS patch, please keep CI matrix minimal. also ensure changelog makes clear it’s type-level + example-level.

Connor O'Brien: decision proposal:
- Python: cut v1.12.0 only (no backport)
- TS: cut v0.23.0 + optional patch backport v0.22.4 for typing mismatch
- Go: cut v0.9.0 only
Any objections?

Dana Lo: no objection. i can prep v0.22.4 cherry-pick for just the typing fix + minimal example fix. will avoid pulling in the whole streaming refactor.

Monica Patel: works for python.

Mateusz Zielinski: works.

Elliot Price: please coordinate timing so docs publish references released versions. docs PRs are queued for early next week.

Connor O'Brien: yup. target schedule:
- TS v0.22.4 (backport) tomorrow EOD
- Python v1.12.0 / TS v0.23.0 / Go v0.9.0 on Monday morning PT
- docs publish after SDK tags land (same day)

release-bot: Release checklist reminder: ensure CHANGELOG updated, tags pushed, GitHub release notes drafted, and downstream docs snippet sync check passing. (ref: redwood#14621)

Wei Chen: one more: docs will include a callout about OpenAI-compat tool-call payload differences. pls don’t claim 1:1 OpenAI streaming semantics in SDK notes.

Ibrahim Khan: +1. in changelog, maybe “OpenAI-compatible mode has minor differences; see docs compatibility note.”

Connor O'Brien: ack. i’ll add a standard line to each release note:
“Note: Tool calling/streaming payloads may differ in OpenAI-compat mode; see docs ‘Compatibility’ section.”

Sabrina James: if anyone wants, i can paste the “known pitfalls” bullets for release notes too (partial args, incremental JSON, disconnect/retry). keeps support happy.

Connor O'Brien: pls do.

Sabrina James: release-note addendum (short):
- Streaming tool call arguments may be delivered across multiple events; buffer/assemble before parsing.
- Structured output is schema-constrained but still validate JSON and retry on parse/validation failures.
- Handle stream disconnects with idempotent retries where possible.

Connor O'Brien: perfect. i’ll compile final release notes and post in #announcements once tags are cut.
